packet: C1-12 LTP feasibility with a real second BPA

host.toolchain: gcc 14.2.0, autoconf 2.72, automake 1.16.5, libtool 2.4.7 (installed for this build)

bp_over_ltp_confirmed_with_ion_utilities.detail: bpsource ipn:2.1 'fn LTP hello' delivered to bpsink on node 2 (12 octets)

receipt_returned_over_bp.reason: ION gives the sender no transport handle to bind to a durable attempt record; the return leg is blocked behind that seam, not attempted

interruption.method: iptables INPUT -i lo -p udp --dport 42113 -j DROP, inserted then deleted by rule; the ruleset is never flushed
interruption.conclusion: LTP resumed the session and repaired the lost red-part segments after the link returned; the ADU arrived intact

expiry.conclusion: the bundle's lifetime elapsed during the outage and it was never delivered; nothing was staged and fn's obligation is untouched by that transport event

blockers.title: ION has no non-destructive receive
blockers.detail: bp_receive() (bpv7/library/libbp.c) deletes the delivery-queue element, zeroes bundle.payload.content, calls bpDestroyBundle() and commits the SDR transaction before returning. After it returns nothing redelivers the ADU. bprecvfile additionally writes testfile<N> with no fsync, no rename, and a per-process counter that restarts at 1.
blockers.consequence: fn's inventory/download/delete contract in tools/run_bp_receive.py cannot be served by ION. An app-level staging copy (tests/ltp/fn_ltp_stage.c) is mandatory, and its delete removes fn's own staged file, never an ION-retained bundle.
blockers.residual: the window between bp_receive()'s commit and the staging fsync cannot be closed with ION's public API; it is covered at the fn layer by durable sender work, retry and receipt idempotence

blockers.title: ION returns no bundle identifier to the sending application
blockers.detail: bpsendfile prints none; bp_send() returns only an in-process SdrObject address for the new bundle.
blockers.consequence: fn's durable attempt record has no observed transport handle to bind. The lab recorded 'ion-unreported:request-ltp'. A real adapter must read the RFC 9171 bundle id out of that SDR object through the C API before the bundle is destroyed.

blockers.title: EID scheme mismatch
blockers.detail: fn's configured peer-eid dtn://fn.lab/inbox is an application identity ACL2 binds inside the request ADU. ION registers the ipn scheme (node.service); an unmapped first run failed with 'bpsendfile: failed to send'. ION does accept the dtn scheme via dtn2fw/dtn2adminep.
blockers.consequence: an ION adapter must carry an explicit application-peer-EID to BP-destination-EID mapping; the pinned dtn7-rs lab conflated the two only because dtn7-rs is natively dtn:-scheme

delegated_to_ion: LTP session establishment, red-part segmentation at 1200 octets, checkpoints, reception reports and retransmission
BP forwarding, duct selection and the contact/range plan
delegated_limits: LTP repair is budgeted: maxTimeouts 5 and maxRepairRounds 8 per session. An outage longer than that budget cancels the session; BPv7 has no custody transfer to recover it, so recovery falls to fn's own durable retry.
sessionInactivityLimit 0 means no inactivity cancellation was configured in this profile
owlt 0 and a 1,000,000 byte/s loopback rate; no real light time, asymmetry or contact schedule was exercised
